newsitem.title: USA: Gillette sues Norelco over ads.
newsitem.headline: Gillette sues Norelco over ads.

text.p: The Gillette Co. said Wednesday that it filed a lawsuit against Norelco Consumer Products Co. in U.S. District Court here, alleging that Norelco used a false and disparaging advertising campaign for its electric razor.
Gillette said the suit, filed on Oct. 9, sought to stop the ads, and asks for punitive and other damages.
The suit alleged Norelco's print and broadcast ad campaign was deceptive in promoting its new electric razor, Gillette said.
John Darman, vice president, business management of Gillette's blades and razors unit, said the advertising was intended to harm the reputation of Gillette and its wet-shaving products.

"Norelco's new advertising takes direct aim at wet-shaving systems, including Gillette products, with a barrage of offensive, exaggerated and distorted statements and images focused on irritation and performance," said Darman.
Connecticut-based Norelco, a unit of Philips Electronics NV, said it could not comment on pending litigation.
Separately, Gillette said it acquired the blade and razor business of Astra a.s., a privately held company in the Czech Republic for an undisclosed price.
Located in Jevicko, Czech Republic, Astra employs about 600 people and produces double edge blades, twin blade cartridges and razors, and disposable razors.
